definition: An echoborg is a person whose words and actions are determined, in whole or in part, by an artificial intelligence (AI).
details: The term echoborg was coined in 2014 by social psychologists Kevin Corti and Alex Gillespie, whose research at the London School of Economics explored unscripted face-to-face social encounters between research participants and confederates whose words were covertly supplied by Cleverbot and spoken with a delay via speech shadowing. The idea is derivative of the cyranoid concept that originated with Stanley Milgram. The echoborg method can show how people behave and make attributions toward an AI (or more precisely, a human-AI hybrid) when their psychological state is fully primed for human–human interaction. Corti and Gillespie argue that other forms of human–AI interaction (e.g., computer-mediated conversation) involve a machine interface, anthropomorphic analog, or a virtual reality layer through which a person communicates with an AI, and that these forms of mediation fundamentally alter the intersubjective relationship between the human and artificial agents party to an interaction. explainer.lead: An echoborg is a person who speaks or acts partly or wholly under an AI’s direction, creating a human–AI hybrid in an otherwise ordinary encounter. The idea helps researchers study how people respond to AI when they believe they are simply interacting with another human.

tiers.eli5: Imagine talking to someone who is secretly repeating whatever a computer tells them to say. The person’s face and voice are real, but the words come from the computer. This lets researchers see how you treat that mix of person and machine when you think you are just having a normal conversation.
tiers.practitioner: The method uses unscripted, face-to-face encounters in which a confederate covertly receives AI-generated wording and delivers it through speech shadowing, with a delay. Corti and Gillespie’s research used Cleverbot and primed participants for human–human interaction. The human intermediary, covert setup, and delivery delay make this different from evaluating a chatbot through a visible interface.
tiers.paperLevel: An echoborg is a human whose words and actions are determined, wholly or partly, by an AI. Kevin Corti and Alex Gillespie coined the term in 2014, deriving it from Stanley Milgram’s cyranoid concept; their London School of Economics research used Cleverbot-supplied speech in face-to-face encounters. The method studies behavior and attributions toward a human–AI hybrid under human–human interaction priming, but its human embodiment and covert, delayed delivery distinguish it from computer-mediated human–AI interaction.

explainer.example: A research participant sits down for an unscripted conversation with a confederate. Unknown to the participant, Cleverbot supplies what the confederate says, and the confederate repeats it aloud after a delay; researchers can then study how the participant behaves while psychologically prepared to talk with another human.

usedIn.name: Social psychology research
usedIn.detail: Used at the London School of Economics to study behavior and attributions in unscripted face-to-face encounters.

usedIn.name: Performance art
usedIn.detail: Used to comment on AI’s growing ubiquity, its contribution to human culture, and human dependency on machines.

explainer.intuition: If an AI’s words arrive through a living person rather than a screen, the interaction can feel socially human even though the machine supplies some or all of the content. That makes the echoborg a way to examine human–AI relations without an obvious machine interface.
howItWorks: Prime a participant for an ordinary human–human encounter.
Have the participant meet a confederate face to face.
Covertly supply the confederate’s words from an AI.
Let the confederate repeat those words through delayed speech shadowing.
Observe the participant’s behavior and attributions toward the hybrid.
explainer.whyItMatters: It separates AI-generated communication from the screens, avatars, and other mediation that usually shape human–AI encounters. It therefore offers a way to study how people behave toward, and make judgments about, a human–AI hybrid during face-to-face interaction.
misconceptions: The echoborg is the person speaking or acting, not the AI supplying the direction.
It does not require a robotic body or implanted machinery.
Direct conversation with a chatbot is not the original echoborg research setup.
